title: Single-coordinate noise semigroup
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with a probability mass function $\pi$. Suppose a finite nonempty index set $\iota$ indexes a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one function as one basis vector. For every $n\ge 0$, coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, real parameters $\rho,\sigma$, and function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, applying the single-coordinate noise operator with parameter $\sigma$ and then with parameter $\rho$ gives the same function as applying it once with parameter $\rho\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite and nonempty, with decidable equality
There is a real basis of functions on $\Omega$ containing the constant-one function and orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
$i$ is a coordinate in the $n$-coordinate product
